subject: biochemistry
title: Immunochemistry: V(D)J recombination, MHC antigen processing, and complement cascades

steps.tx: Antibody diversity is generated during lymphocyte development by somatic **V(D)J recombination**. The recombination activating gene products RAG-1 and RAG-2 introduce double-strand DNA breaks at recombination signal sequences flanking variable, diversity, and joining gene segments. Non-homologous end joining repairs the breaks, during which terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase (**TdT**) randomly inserts template-independent N-nucleotides, creating immense junctional diversity within complementarity-determining regions.
steps.say: Antibody diversity arises through somatic V(D)J recombination driven by RAG-1 and RAG-2. Terminal deoxynucleotidyl transferase inserts random nucleotides at junctions, creating billions of unique antigen receptor combinations.

steps.tx: Antigen presentation is mediated by two distinct classes of major histocompatibility complex (**MHC**) proteins. MHC Class I molecules, expressed on all nucleated cells, present endogenous cytoplasmic peptides to CD8+ cytotoxic T-lymphocytes. Endogenous proteins are degraded by the proteasome and transported into the endoplasmic reticulum via **TAP** (transporter associated with antigen processing). MHC Class II molecules, restricted to professional antigen-presenting cells, present exogenous endocytosed antigens to CD4+ helper T-cells.
steps.say: MHC Class I displays endogenous cytosolic antigens processed by proteasomes and loaded via TAP to CD8 cytotoxic T-cells. MHC Class II on dendritic cells and macrophages presents endocytosed exogenous peptides to CD4 helper T-cells.

steps.tx: The **complement** system comprises three converging cascades: classical, lectin, and alternative pathways. The classical pathway is triggered when C1q binds antigen-antibody complexes (IgM or IgG). The lectin pathway activates via mannose-binding lectin binding microbial carbohydrates. The alternative pathway spontaneously hydrolyzes C3 (tick-over). All pathways converge to generate **C3 convertase**, which cleaves C3 into anaphylatoxin C3a and opsonin C3b. C3b initiates C5 convertase to assemble the membrane attack complex (C5b-9).
steps.say: Complement activates through classical, lectin, and alternative pathways. All pathways converge on C3 convertase to generate opsonin C3b and anaphylatoxin C3a. C5 convertase then launches the membrane attack complex C5b-9 to lyse targets.

rows: IgM or IgG bound to antigen (C1qrs)
Mannose-binding lectin bound to pathogen mannose

C5 convertase cleaves C5 into C5a + C5b

steps.tx: Regulatory complement proteins prevent host bystander lysis. Decay-accelerating factor (CD55) and CD59 (protectin) are anchored to host erythrocyte membranes via **GPI** anchors. CD55 accelerates convertase decay, while CD59 blocks membrane attack complex assembly. In paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, acquired PIGA mutations prevent GPI anchor synthesis, leaving red cells vulnerable to complement-mediated intravascular hemolysis, thrombosis, and dark morning hemoglobinuria.
steps.say: Host cells express GPI-anchored CD55 and CD59 to inhibit complement attack. Acquired PIGA mutations cause paroxysmal nocturnal hemoglobinuria, lacking CD55 and CD59, causing episodic complement-mediated hemolytic anemia and thrombosis.

nodes.label: Acquired somatic PIGA mutation in HSC
